transcript.text: My Panasonic NN-ST45KWBPQ is sparking inside when I heat soup, little blue flashes on the right-hand wall and a crackling noise. I stopped it. Is it safe?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Stop using the microwave now: switch it off at the socket and unplug it, and don't run it again (not even empty) until we know why it sparked. Never take the outer casing off — parts inside can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged. Sparking inside a microwave indicates an electrical arc that can damage the magnetron or cause a fire. You must unplug the appliance immediately and do not attempt to run it. The most likely cause for blue flashes on the right-hand wall while heating soup is a burnt or damaged 'waveguide cover' (the small rectangular panel on the side wall) or food splatter that has carbonised. Once you have unplugged it, please check if there is any obvious food residue on that right-hand wall panel and whether the panel itself looks scorched or has holes in it.

Ok, it's unplugged. There's a cardboard-like panel on the right wall with a black burnt spot on it and greasy splatter around it. I also noticed a slight burnt smell and one wisp of smoke from that spot earlier, which stopped when I switched it off.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. That suggests the issue: the 'cardboard-like' panel is the waveguide cover, and the black burnt spot means it has been arcing (sparking) repeatedly. This carbonised area acts like a magnet for electricity, causing those blue flashes and crackling noises. While replacing the waveguide cover is often a simple fix, the arcing may have damaged the cavity lining or even the magnetron (the part that generates the heat). Please contact Panasonic support or a local authorised repair service. Do not try to clean off the burn marks with abrasive pads, as this will likely make the problem worse.

candidates: Burnt or damaged waveguide cover (mica sheet) (high)
Food splatter or residue on the cavity wall (medium)
